commit.message: perf(ci): run pytest once during Magi verification

specification.objective: MAGI-020: remove duplicated pytest execution from ./verify.sh while preserving standalone test and coverage scripts, coverage threshold and Hermes plugin validation; quantify elapsed time against measured baseline.

requirements.statement: Execute the Magi pytest suite exactly once within ./verify.sh, through ci/coverage.sh with branch and production coverage; preserve correct process exit status.
Preserve independent bash ci/test.sh and bash ci/coverage.sh for manual and POLIS use, Python compile checks, production coverage >90%, and Hermes plugins validate --install-deps.
Document measured before/after end-to-end verify.sh duration, failure propagation and limitations without Magi version bump.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Behavioral isolated shell regression confirms verify.sh invokes exactly one pytest command while retaining compile, coverage and Hermes validation.
Regression proves failed pytest and below-threshold production coverage cause nonzero verify.sh exits, with manual ci/test.sh unchanged.
Full ./verify.sh and POLIS gates pass, baseline duration is contrasted with observed post-change time, and changelog/README updated.

invariants.statement: Plugin version stays 1.7.8; Hermes APIs, tests for Magi core and plugin and coverage denominator stay unchanged.

forbidden_states.statement: verify.sh invokes both ci/test.sh and ci/coverage.sh, or swallows failures.

inputs.statement: Baseline d9c72a8 verify.sh 38.66 seconds; after MAGI-013 a4c5b41 verify.sh 36.73 seconds, both with two pytest invocations.

outputs.statement: Single-test-pass verify.sh, dedicated shell integration tests and 1.7.8 docs.

failure_semantics.statement: Propagate nonzero pytest and production coverage gate failures; do not claim stable speedup from single noisy run.
